messages.subject: linear regression - generated quantities
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to build a simple linear regression model in stan. 

I would like to keep track (predcheck) where ypred is bigger than y. And, also calculate y for a value of  x_new. I am getting compiler error for the below code. Any suggestions on what's wrong?

scode = "data {
  int n;
  vector[n] x; // predictor matrix
  vector[n] y; // outcome vector
  vector[n] yrep; // prediction vector
  real x_new;
  vector[n] mu;
  real y_tilde;
}
parameters {
  real alpha; // intercept
  real beta; // coefficients for predictors
  real<lower=0> sigma; // error scale
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(40,100);
  beta ~ normal(0,30);
  sigma ~ gamma(1,0.001);
  y ~ normal((x -mean(x))* beta + alpha, sigma); 
  yrep ~ normal((x -mean(x))* beta + alpha,sigma);
}
generated quantities {
  vector[n] predcheck;
  for (i in 1:n)
    predcheck[i] <- step(yrep[i] - y[i]);
  y_tilde <- normal_rng(alpha + beta * x_new, sigma);
}"
fit1 <- stan(model_code = scode,data=list(x=c(23.9,43.3,36.3,40.6,57,52.5,46.1,142,112.6,23.7),
            y=c(41,52,18.7,55,40,29.2,51,17.6,46.6,57),n=10, x.new = 46.1),iter=1000,verbose=FALSE)
print(fit1,digits=4)
plot(fit1)

Error:
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'e3416d6e942f2a2736d01252bc7c3ce0' with error message:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

attempt to assign variable in wrong block. left-hand-side variable origin=data

ERROR at line 27

 25:      for (i in 1:n)
 26:        predcheck[i] <- step(yrep[i] - y[i]);
 27:      y_tilde <- normal_rng(alpha + beta * x_new, sigma);
                    ^
 28:    }

PARSER EXPECTED: <expression assignable to left-hand side>

messages.subject: Re: linear regression - generated quantities
parts:
On Monday, November 9, 2015 at 8:54:37 PM UTC-5, Neerav Shah wrote:
Any suggestions on what's wrong?

attempt to assign variable in wrong block. left-hand-side variable origin=data

You have to declare y_tilde inside generated quantities rather than data. The things you declare in the data block are what you conditioning on.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: linear regression - generated quantities
parts:
On Tuesday, November 10, 2015 at 6:15:47 AM UTC-5, Neerav Shah wrote:
Thanks for responding, Ben.

I moved  y_tilde to generated quantities. Another question I have is, where should the declaration/calculattion of predcheck happen?

Not in the data block, which as I said previously, is only for things that you condition on. Hence, it is impossible to change the values to them every iteration of the Markov Chain. I am not entirely sure what you are trying to do but it looks as if only n, x, y, and x_new should be in data and everything else should be in generated quantities. What is the distinction between y_rep and y_tilde in your Stan program?

Ben
